title: Smallest K-Length Subsequence With Occurrences of a Letter
summary: Given a string s, an integer k, a letter letter, and an integer repetition, find the lexicographically smallest subsequence of length k that contains the letter letter at least repetition times.
statement: Given a string s, an integer k, a letter letter, and an integer repetition, find the lexicographically smallest subsequence of length k that contains the letter letter at least repetition times. Ensure the letter appears in s at least repetition times. A subsequence is formed by removing characters from s while maintaining the order of the remaining characters. A string a is lexicographically smaller than string b if the first differing character in a and b corresponds to a letter that precedes b's in the alphabet.
constraints: Return the lexicographically smallest length-k subsequence containing letter at least repetition times.
The input guarantees enough occurrences of letter.
hints: A monotonic stack gives lexical minimality, but capacity and required-letter reservations constrain pops and pushes.
Pop larger characters only when enough total positions remain and any popped required letter can be replaced later.
Track letters_left and needed; reserve needed of the remaining k-stack slots, and adjust needed when required letters enter or leave.
The stack exchange makes each prefix smallest among feasible completions; the two feasibility counts guarantee length and repetition can still be met.
